newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hundreds stranded in Philippine transport strike.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds stranded in Philippine transport strike.

text.p: Hundreds of commuters in two southern Philippine cities were stranded on Friday after drivers of public vehicles refused to ply their routes in protest against a recent oil price increase.
Police said the strike almost paralysed transportation in Davao and Butuan cities.
The rest of the country, including the capital Manila, was partially affected, they said.

In Davao city, all schools were closed and only half the business establishments opened as 90 percent of public sector drivers went on strike, police officer Nelson Latua said in a telephone interview.
Radio reports said 90 percent of public transportation was also crippled in the southern Butuan city.
The strike left normally congested Metro Manila a quieter place.
"It is one smooth joy ride to the city," one female commuter said.
The various transport operators and labour unions, which joined forces in a group called Campaign Against Oil Price Increase, planned a mid-day rally in the city.

The Philippines' three oil refiners raised petroleum product prices by as much as five percent on August 1, saying their crude import costs had risen after the peso was effectively devalued last month.
An official at the Metro Manila Development Authority (MMDA) said the government had pressed about 40 trucks into service to ferry passengers in the city.
The Education Department suspended classes in the primary and secondary levels early on Friday in anticipation of the strike.
The strike had so far been peaceful and there were no reports of trouble, the police said.
